# dsh-subagent-codex-pro
English | 中文

A Codex delegation tool that can carry **a model and a reasoning effort per
call** — the two things
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-codex` cannot express.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## 0.8.0 integration and migration

The plugin now exposes a versioned machine API and CLI for
orchestrators, alongside its DSH tool/pro

vider. Both use the same supervised
Codex app-server runner. See the Flywheel, preparation and PR gu

r. Both use the same supervised
Codex app-server runner. See the Flywheel, preparation and PR guide.

The default permission is now **workspace-write + never**. Existing profiles
that explicitly configu

red full access keep that explicit choice; profiles that
omitted it receive the new bounded default.

Per-call overrides can narrow the
configured policy, not silently expand it. Required effective con

figuration
fields must be present and match before a task is sent. DSH provider/maxTokens
overrides
that this Codex backend cannot honor are rejected.

The complete machine receipt includes configuration, effort-request evidence,
usage completeness, ac

tual process facts and cleanup. DSH Host results retain
the official narrow shape. Full details neve
r require parsing the diagnostic log.
## The gap this fills

`subagent_codex`'s schema exposes only `description` and `prompt`, so a caller
cannot name a model o

r a thinking level. In a recorded session a model asked to
do exactly that tried the obvious thing a

vel. In a recorded session a model asked to
do exactly that tried the obvious thing and was refused:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The chain, from the harness source:

The Codex protocol supports the choices this package exposes: `model` and the
unattended permission

policy on `thread/start`, model/cwd/permission overrides on
`thread/resume` (0.165+), and `effort` p

er turn on `turn/start`. The official
provider never sends them. Reported upstream:
<https://github.
com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/9115>

There is a second, separate defect: enabling `modelSelectionSettings: true` on a
row whose provider

is external (`codex-pro`) makes that row **silently**
register no tool at all — no error, no log, no

failed-preset badge. A control row
identical except for the flag registers normally. Also in that r

d-preset badge. A control row
identical except for the flag registers normally. Also in that report.
## How this works instead
Two layers, both under this package's control.
### Execution: the same protocol the official provider speaks

`src/wire.ts` and `src/run.ts` are a port of the official app-server adapter —
the initialize handsh

ake, the ephemeral thread, thread/turn association
including notifications that arrive before `turn/

start` returns, unattended
approval decisions, and terminal-answer selection by phase — with these
a

turns, unattended
approval decisions, and terminal-answer selection by phase — with these
additions:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Neither literal appears anywhere in the official adapter's 871 lines. A thinking
level is a `turn/st

art` field, not a `thread/start` field in 0.165/0.166; the
thread-time default is left to Codex. Two

mechanical differences from the source: the JSON-RPC transport is this package's
own (`src/jsonrpc.

ts`), and the app-server is started as
`<command> app-server --stdio` from `PATH` rather than from `

`'s
manifest. `src/codex-exec.ts`, the earlier `codex exec` path, is retained and
tested but unused.

The executable is the `command` setting (default `codex`), resolved through the
Host's `PATH` — and

the desktop app captures that environment when it launches.
A Node version switch, or any change to

the login shell, can leave the global
install out of it. When that happens, set `command` to an abso

lute path: the
official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-codex` bundle ships a pinned executable

## Capabilities
| | status |

| `model` / `reasoning_effort` per call | ✅ |
| final message returned | ✅ |
| images the run produc

ed (screenshots, viewed files) | ✅ when the calling model route accepts images |
| images handed to

the run (`images`, absolute paths) | ✅ |
| schema-enforced answer (`output_schema`, or the harness's

row setting) | ✅ verified locally |
| `run_in_background` + progress via `job_output` | ✅ |
| read-

only review permission (`read-only`) | ✅ `approvalPolicy=never` + `sandbox=read-only` |
| token usag
e / model context window | ✅ public machine receipt + internal outcome; DSH result/tool/job contract

s retain their official shapes |
| account rate limits | ✅ separate from token usage; included in th

e public machine receipt |
| process-range cleanup with confirmation | ✅ POSIX; unconfirmed is repor

ted |
| deadline covers startup and turn; user cancel distinct | ✅ |
| app-server protocol (handshak

e, thread lifecycle, approval decisions) | ✅ |
| interactive approvals | by design none — a delegate

d run is unattended, as the official provider is |
| continuable / thread reuse | ✅ `session` reuses

one; `thread_id` continues any |
| `maxDepth` / persona / `toolFilter` | ❌ not applicable — see bel

; `thread_id` continues any |
| `maxDepth` / persona / `toolFilter` | ❌ not applicable — see below |
The three refusals above are not gaps to be filled. A Codex delegation is a **leaf**: it has no DSH

child
agent, so a delegation-depth cap has nothing to cap. Its tools are Codex's own — the shell, th

e patch tool, its
own MCP servers — not this harness's, so a **tool filter**, which names DSH tools,

cannot describe them; restrict
Codex through its own configuration instead. And a **persona** is a

system instruction for a child agent, where
this one already takes the task in `prompt`. Declaring a

ny of them `true` would promise the harness an
enforcement that does not exist.

Use the official provider when its configuration and result contract meet your
needs. This package a

dds per-call configuration and a public machine receipt
for external orchestrators. Its compatibilit

y is checked against the documented
DSH/Codex baselines; new upstream releases still require contrac

ainst the documented
DSH/Codex baselines; new upstream releases still require contract verification.
